events.text: Case opened: Death at the Meridian Observatory

At 23:40 on Saturday night, security guard Nell Okafor found the observatory's director, Dr. Elias Voss (58), dead on the floor of the main dome beneath the telescope gantry. The donor gala had been running in the hall next door since 19:00. Voss was last seen leaving the hall at about 22:25. First responders assumed a fall on the gantry stairs. Three people had reason to quarrel with him that night: his deputy director Dr. Mara Quill, his doctoral student Theo Lark, and board chairman and principal donor Gideon Ashby. The dome corridor camera was not recording. Whether this is an accident or a homicide — and who, if anyone, should answer for it — is for the investigation to establish.
Set out how I intend to run this.

Dr. Elias Voss left the hall alive and was found dead a little over an hour later. I want that window accounted for by records before I listen to anyone's version of it: doors, cameras, the scene itself. Dr. Mara Quill, Theo Lark, Gideon Ashby — three people with a quarrel is three stories to test, not three suspects. Nobody is the answer yet.
Flag the easy assumption.

I'll say this once: "he fell" is a conclusion, not an observation. I need the body position documented, the post-mortem ordered, and every exhibit sealed with continuity. Send me what you find and I'll tell you what it shows — and what it doesn't.
Tell the team what a charge needs.
Bring me a story a jury can feel: who wanted Elias Voss dead, who was close enough to do it, and one exhibit I can hold up in closing. Get me that and I'll do the rest.

events.text: Name every doubt the record supports.

Members of the jury, the question is not whether Dr. Mara Quill could have done this. It is whether the prosecution has made you sure. The fingerprints on the gantry rail: theo operates the telescope from that gantry most nights. Fingerprints cannot be dated. The voss's mobile phone: the Ashby text does not say what 'this' refers to, and the draft email was never sent. The grant account ledger: irregular bookkeeping is not evidence of violence; many people had access to the finance system. The admin console audit log: her password was on a note under her keyboard; the log proves the account, not the person. Meanwhile the evidence about Theo Lark — his are the only identifiable prints on the rail Voss went over — was never answered. Each of those gaps is a reasonable doubt, and the law says what you do with a reasonable doubt. Not guilty.

events.text: Dr. Mara Quill pushed Elias Voss over the upper gantry rail at about 22:50. Over three years she had diverted 240,000 of grant money to a shell company registered to her sister-in-law. Voss found the hole in the accounts, told her on Saturday afternoon that he would lay it before the board on Monday, and went up to the dome after the speeches. She had already switched off the corridor camera. She left the archive room, let herself into the dome with her override card, and asked him for time. He refused. In the struggle on the gantry he tore the fringe of her shawl; she pushed him. She buried the shawl in the archive bin and was back in the hall for the 23:20 group photograph.

data.method: A push over the upper gantry rail during a confrontation she had arranged to be unobserved.
